problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=9{e}^{-3t}-4{e}^{-t}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=1\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$

Question 10
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=9e−3t−4e−t, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=1m/s when t=0s, find the velocity (in m/s) of the particle at time t.

a
 v(t)=4−3e−2t
b
 v(t)=4e−t−27e−3t+24
c
 v(t)=4e−2t−27e−4t+24
d
v(t)=4e−t−3e−3t+1
e
 v(t)=4e−t−3e−3t
